title: GitOps Continuous Deployment Controller with Automated Drift Self-Healing
problem: Kubernetes cluster state frequently diverges from intended Git configuration due to manual emergency kubectl interventions, failing CI/CD pipeline synchronizations, and unrecorded environment adjustments. When production state is not immutably committed to version control, disaster recovery becomes impossible and infrastructure security degrades. This project implements a lightweight GitOps continuous deployment controller from first principles in Go. The controller watches target Git manifest repositories, renders Helm templates and plain YAML manifests, applies declarative state via the Kubernetes dynamic client, detects live out-of-band cluster drift in real-time, executes automated self-healing reconciliation loops, and spins up isolated ephemeral preview namespaces for incoming pull requests.
use_cases: Enterprise platform engineering teams enforcing declarative infrastructure-as-code state across Kubernetes clusters
Automated drift detection and self-healing systems reverting unauthorized manual cluster mutations
Continuous preview environment controllers provisioning ephemeral pull request testing namespaces
hard_parts: Managing three-way declarative merge patch calculations between Git desired state, live cluster state, and last-applied annotations
Implementing efficient non-blocking reconciliation worker queues with exponential backoff and rate-limiting
Detecting out-of-band live resource drift and executing safe self-healing mutations without service disruption
Managing ephemeral Kubernetes namespace lifecycles with automated TTL expiration and garbage collection
screener_signals: Modular Go implementation cleanly separating Git pollers, Helm template renderers, dynamic K8s clients, and drift reconcilers
Automated chaos test injecting manual cluster modifications and verifying automated self-healing restoration within 15 seconds
Anti-fake verification script committing dynamic deployment manifests to Git and asserting exact Kubernetes replica convergence

components.name: Helm Template Expansion Engine

components.name: Kubernetes Dynamic Resource Reconciler
components.purpose: Applies manifests using Kubernetes dynamic client and three-way strategic merge patch algorithms

components.name: Drift Detection & Self-Healing Watcher
components.purpose: Listens to Kubernetes informers, detects live state deviations from Git, and triggers restorative reconciliations

architecture.data_flow: The Git Poller watches designated Git branches for commit updates; when a commit arrives, the Helm Expansion Engine renders chart templates into concrete manifests; the Dynamic Resource Reconciler compares desired manifests with live cluster state; resources are created or updated using three-way strategic merge patching; Kubernetes Informers continuously monitor live cluster state; if manual kubectl changes alter replicas or configurations out-of-band, the Drift Watcher flags state divergence and re-applies Git truth within 15 seconds.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Continuous reconciliation loops overriding unauthorized out-of-band mutations; admission webhooks verifying signed Git commit SHAs.

worksheet.q1: Core deliverable: a GitOps continuous deployment controller in Go with Git poller, Helm renderer, dynamic K8s client, and drift self-healing.
worksheet.q2: Target users: platform engineers, Kubernetes infrastructure specialists, and SREs.
worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: declarative cluster state enforcement, automated drift self-healing, and ephemeral PR preview environments.
worksheet.q4: Stated hours: 39 hours. Calculated bottom-up: 34 component hours * 1.15 buffer = 39.1 -> 39 hours. Advanced level.
worksheet.q5: Hard parts: three-way merge patch calculations, non-blocking reconciler worker queues, real-time drift detection, and namespace lifecycle GC.
worksheet.q6: Starter input: 50 Kubernetes resource manifests across 5 application stacks with Helm charts. Synthetic configurations only.
worksheet.q7: Hardware: Linux/macOS/Windows WSL2, 8GB RAM, CPU only, $0 cost, zero cloud accounts. Fallback: mock Kubernetes API server.
worksheet.q8: Riskiest component: Infinite reconciliation loops on dynamic fields. Fallback: filter managed dynamic fields during diff calculation.
worksheet.q9: Potential faking: static reconciliation logs. Anti-fake check 5 commits dynamic ConfigMap to Git at runtime and asserts live cluster convergence.
worksheet.q10: Safety/ethics: Safe; local Kind/K3s container cluster only, no cloud production credentials.
